page.title: Single sign-on
page.description: Let people sign in through your identity provider with SAML 2.0, map directory groups to roles, and decide whether local passwords still work.

setupBanner.title: Finish setup first
setupBanner.masterKey: SAML needs the control plane master key to keep its signing key. Configure the master key, then come back.
setupBanner.baseUrl: SAML needs an https dashboard URL, because identity providers post sign-in responses to it. Set one under Settings, General.

list.title: SAML connections
list.description: Each connection trusts one identity provider. Enabled connections show a button on the sign-in page.
list.emptyBody: Add one for Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak or any SAML 2.0 identity provider.

form.sheetDescription: Give these service provider values to your identity provider, then import its metadata.
form.name: Display name
form.nameHelp: Shown on the sign-in button, for example the company or IdP name.

sp.title: Service provider details
sp.description: Copy these into the SAML app you create at your identity provider.
sp.saveFirst: Save the connection to get its URLs.

import.title: Import IdP metadata
import.description: Paste the metadata URL or XML from your identity provider. This fills the entity ID, sign-in URL and signing certificate, taking the newest one valid today when the metadata lists several.
import.done: Metadata imported. Review and enable the connection.

idp.title: Identity provider
idp.description: Filled by the import, or enter them by hand. Responses must be signed by this certificate.
idp.certificatesHelp: One certificate. When the identity provider rotates its key, paste or import the new certificate at the switch.

access.title: Accounts and roles
access.description: Decide who may sign in and which role they get.
access.jitHelp: Off: only people who already have an account here can sign in.
access.syncRoles: Apply the mapped role on every sign-in
access.syncRolesHelp: Group changes at the identity provider take effect at the next sign-in. People in no mapped group get the default role, or are refused without one.
access.defaultRoleNone: None: refuse people in no mapped group
access.domainsHelp: Comma separated, for example example.com. Empty allows any domain.

attributes.title: Attribute names
attributes.description: Leave empty to use the common Okta, Entra ID and Keycloak names.
attributes.name: Display name attribute

form.deleteBody: People linked through this connection keep their accounts but can no longer sign in with it.

mappings.title: Group to role mappings
mappings.description: When someone signs in, or a directory group changes, the highest priority matching group decides their role. Group names match case-insensitively.
mappings.empty: No mappings. Everyone gets the connection's default role.

enforce.title: Require single sign-on
enforce.description: Refuse password, passkey and email code sign-in for everyone except root users.
enforce.label: Require SSO for non-root users
enforce.breakGlass: Root users keep their password as the break-glass path, and recover-admin on the host still resets it. See the emergency access docs.

spCert.title: Service provider certificate
spCert.description: Generated on first use. Some identity providers ask for it to verify signed requests or encrypt assertions.
spCert.none: Not available until the control plane master key is configured.

scim.title: Directory sync (SCIM)
scim.description: Let your identity provider create, update and deactivate accounts and groups. Deactivating someone there ends their sessions here at once.
scim.defaultRoleHelp: Used when no group mapping matches. With group mappings, directory group changes update roles right away.
scim.empty: No SCIM token yet. Create one and paste it into your identity provider.
scim.revokeBody: Provisioning with this token stops immediately.
scim.shownOnceBody: It is shown once and stored only as a hash. Paste it into the SCIM settings of your identity provider.

policy.title: Session policy
policy.description: Per-team rules every request is checked against: idle timeout, maximum session age, allowed networks and required two-factor sign-in. People in several teams get the strictest combination.
policy.recoveryBody: On the host, run levelrail access-policy-reset --yes to remove every session policy, then sign in again. Saving a policy that would block your own address is refused.
policy.idleHelp: End sessions unused for this long, for example 30m. At least 5m. Empty turns it off.
policy.maxAgeHelp: End sessions older than this, for example 12h. At least 15m. Empty turns it off.
policy.maxSessionsHelp: Most full sessions one person may hold at once, across browsers and devices. 0 turns the cap off.
policy.onLimitHelp: Checked on the first request after sign-in or the two-factor step, then every 30 seconds. Sessions over the cap end with a clear message.
policy.allowlistHelp: One IP address or CIDR per line. Applies to sessions and API tokens. Empty allows any address.
policy.requireMfaHelp: People without an authenticator app or passkey can only enroll one until they do. SAML sign-ins count, since the identity provider handles MFA.

oidc.title: OAuth and OIDC sign-in
oidc.description: The same controls as SAML for the providers you enabled under Settings, OAuth sign-in: which groups earn which role, whether a first sign-in creates an account, and which email domains may sign in.
oidc.emptyTitle: No OAuth or OIDC provider yet
oidc.emptyBody: Enable a provider under Settings, OAuth sign-in. It shows up here with its sign-in policy.

form.title: Sign-in policy for {{name}}
form.sheetDescription: Group to role mappings are shared with SAML and directory sync: edit them in the mappings card on this page.

access.title: Access
access.description: Least privilege by default: unknown people are refused, and nobody gets more than the role you pick here.

form.jit: Create an account on first sign-in
form.jitHelp: Off: someone with no account here is refused unless you invited them first. On: the first sign-in creates an account with the mapped role, or the default role.
form.syncRoles: Reapply the mapped role on every sign-in
form.syncRolesHelp: Off: a role is only set when the account is created. On: it follows the groups at each sign-in, and downgrades are written to the audit log. Root users are never changed.
form.defaultRoleHelp: For people none of the mappings match. A role that holds root is never offered: a sign-in claim cannot grant it.
form.domainsHelp: Comma separated, for example example.com. Only these domains can sign in, and the sign-in page sends them to this provider. Empty allows any domain and turns routing off.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Where this provider says which groups a person is in.
groups.unsupported: This provider sends no verified ID token to read groups from, so everyone gets the default role. Use the generic OpenID Connect provider with your identity provider to map groups.

form.groupsClaimHelp: The ID token claim that lists group names, for example groups, roles or realm_access.roles. Only the signed ID token is read.

test.hint: A test login signs you in at the provider and shows what a sign-in would do. It creates no account, role or session. Save your changes first.

accountState.new_account: a new account would be created
accountState.not_provisioned: none, and account creation is off

issue.no_groups_claim: The ID token has no "{{claim}}" claim, so everyone gets the default role. Add a groups claim to the ID token at your identity provider.
issue.wrong_claim_name: The ID token has no "{{claim}}" claim, but it carries a list called "{{value}}".
issue.email_unverified: The provider did not mark this email as verified, so sign-in is refused. Verify the address at the provider.
issue.domain_not_allowed: This email domain is not in the allowed list.
issue.not_provisioned: No account exists for this person and account creation is off.
issue.role_grants_root: The role this sign-in would get holds root, or no longer exists. A claim can never grant root.
issue.no_email: The provider sent no email address.

test.fixed: Policy updated. Run the test again.
test.failedTitle: The test login did not finish
test.failedBody: The provider or the redirect failed (code {{code}}). Check the client ID, client secret and redirect URL, then try again.
test.nothingCreated: Nothing was created: no account, role or session.

test.hint: Opens the real sign-in at your identity provider and shows what it sent and what a sign-in would do. It creates no account, role or session. Save your changes first.
test.fixed: Connection updated. Run the test again.

issue.no_groups_claim: The response carries no "{{attribute}}" attribute, so everyone gets the default role. Add a group attribute statement at your identity provider and set its name as the groups attribute.
issue.domain_not_allowed: This email domain is not claimed by the connection.
issue.not_provisioned: No account exists for this person and account creation is off.
issue.role_grants_root: The role this sign-in would get holds root, or no longer exists. A claim can never grant root.
issue.no_email: The response carried no email address. Check the email attribute name and the NameID format.
issue.wrong_claim_name: The response carries no "{{attribute}}" attribute. Check the groups attribute name against what the identity provider sends.
issue.email_unverified: The identity provider did not vouch for this email address.

clock_skew.title: Clock skew
clock_skew.step: The assertion was outside its validity window. Check that the clocks of this server and the identity provider agree within three minutes (NTP), then try again.

audience_mismatch.title: Audience mismatch
audience_mismatch.step: The identity provider addressed another service provider. Set its audience (entity ID) to {{entityId}} and its ACS URL to {{acs}}.

signature_invalid.title: Signature invalid
signature_invalid.step: The assertion is not signed by the certificate on file. Import the identity provider metadata again, and make sure it signs the assertion, not only the response.

request_mismatch.title: Response does not match the request
request_mismatch.step: The response answered another request or destination. Start the test again from this page, and check the ACS URL {{acs}} at the identity provider.

response_invalid.title: Response refused
response_invalid.step: The response could not be verified. Check the identity provider logs, then import its metadata again.

saml_unavailable.title: Sign-in is not available
saml_unavailable.step: SAML needs an https dashboard URL and the control plane master key. Fix both under Settings, General, then try again.
